cp2.author: Claude H-NETLIST sub-agent cp2 (host face + programme targets + status)

rules: no stubs / shells / tied ports: an input without a real producer stays undriven and is listed in a gap
on-die edges fixed-slot: ready_or_credit only with allowed_exception at the HBM PHY/controller boundary
clock/reset ports are bound to hb_ckgen domain outputs (die CTS / staged reset tree build the trees)
off-die pins (SerDes/UCIe PMA, refclk, por_n) are die top-level ports

notes.cp1: ONE new master ot_static_cmd_target (MODE 0 run collar for 32 svg, MODE 1 command calendar for 4 x-load + 4 DMA) + the existing ot_static_program_target for the 4 VM calendars. All collars take the raw host F20 broadcast; every input is pin-flopped and every output is a flop (owner 19:50). Fixed latencies: cfg row -> target window write 2 edges after cfg_v at the collar pin; launch_v -> run_v 2 edges; MODE 1: a table entry fires (cmd_v at the collar pin) when the exported cycle == C + 2 + LEAD(8) + loop*period + at, C = cycle value in the launch_v pin cycle; x-load / DMA add their own command-pin edge on top (cl2 ctl cmd_v pin flop; DMA DESC_LAT4). Table read is one entry per 3 edges sustained (2-deep prefetch: 2 back-to-back after a gap); a command whose cycle passes before it reaches the head is a sticky FAULT, never a late issue (static schedule, no ready/credit). Status: each collar exports configured/fault/active (status_outputs); cp2 joins them into the ingress block_ready/program_active/program_fault. Physical: the 256-b cfg_data broadcast now has ~48 more sinks (44 collars + COLL); it is install-time only but single-cycle at 1.2 GHz, so the parent must give it a pipelined relay tree (fixed edges, the collars are edge-count agnostic: install latency only). No target RTL changed (svg/calendar/xload/DMA tiles untouched; no re-closure). Bench: rtl/hbm_accel/host_static_20261015/tb_static_cmd_target.sv.
cp2: collar row map: 0x000 programme (sequential per space), 0x800 operand rows, 0xC00 record rows, 0xE00 space/page select, 0xE01 install need + wait-done
hc: Closes G-HC (lg_<q>_2 local_rq/local_wq, 8 ports / 9,536 bits): the far HC tap is driven by a static HC quadrant client hc_<q> (new master ot_hbm_hc_q_static x4) through 16 bank-pair pin-register leaves hc_<q><k> (existing ot_hgi_sfu_lg_pair_leaf). lg_<q>_2 local_rr/local_w_done are now consumed. local_read/local_write stay driven by calendar_<q>; the compiler programmes calendar_<q> and hc_<q> on the same edges (the tap faults on any disagreement).

Programme: hc_<q> owns a 1024x256 programme SRAM (ot_vms_calendar_static W79), loaded and launched by hc_tgt_<q> = ot_static_program_target TARGET 108..111 from host_cp_ingress (F20). TARGET_MASK of host_cp_ingress must admit 108..111 (cp owner).

Fixed added latency vs the codex direct-tap engine: +1 output pin, +1 pair leaf, +1 pair leaf return, +1 input pin => residual capture 23 (was 19), gathered response phase 23 (was 19), write-done 19 edges after the store output edge.
host_completion: Four VM HBM-fill calendars use existing ot_static_program_target PCW10, TARGET56..59. Host status uses one existing parameterised pin-registered join for all67 admitted targets; no empty-participation child join can veto a launch. Native physical timing/placement remains open.

It is lifted leaf-by-leaf: host_N (the granted ot_pdie_ucie macro) + host_cp_ep_face/host_cp_ep (hfd_lk_ep is a wires-only wrapper over inout die buses, lifted to its two leaves) + host_cp_landing + host_cp_packet in the host_cp window + host_cp_ingress. hfd_host_native's glue (6-bit tx credit counter, zero pads, pad_fault, fault concat) has no die home -> gaps G-HOST-TXCREDIT / G-HOST-PAD / G-STATUS; session id has no producer (G-HOST-SESSION); the loader service face of the packet engine (h_*/h_dma_*/m_*/irq/fault) belonged to the retired dynamic loader/CP (G-HOST-LOADERFACE).

AXI-lite valid/ready between host_cp_packet and host_cp_ingress is treated as part of the off-die host boundary (README: "host elasticity ends at configuration writes"); nothing after the ingress uses ready/credit.

notes.idxcoll:
KEY LINES (G-CIL-IDXKEY / G-SMVM-KEYSTAGE): the service key staging producer IS the stack's eight SM service groups (their landing + canonical-row SRAMs are the staging). hb_idx.key_lines[j*8792 + p*1099 +: 1099] = svg_

.sm_packet, field order permuted by wires ({valid,tag10,data1088} MSB-first -> [0] valid, [10:1] tag, [1098:11] pair). Two RTL changes make it exact (both in this branch, bench rtl/test/hbm_idx_static/run_idx_key_service.sh PASS + 4 mutants FAIL): (1) ot_hbm_idx_score_static tag check (128*p + beat) % 1024 = the packed136 service tag tag_base+row with tag_base = 128*p + block first beat (the old (beat*8+p) % 1024 cannot be produced by any sequential-tag service block); tools/hbm_idx_static_parent_vectors.py follows. (2) ot_hbm_svc_sm_issuer / ot_hbm_svc_sm_group parameter FIXED_GO (default 0 = unchanged event go): with FIXED_GO=1 the programme go is the descriptor's compiler slot go_at [142:119] (missed slot = sticky fault, never waits). MEASURED: with the event go the eight groups of one stack start 0..20 edges apart (HBM residency), so key beats are not aligned and the scorer faults; with FIXED_GO=1 skew 0, 128 beats exact, scorer fault 0. => the die must instantiate svg_ with FIXED_GO=1 (engine_region, VMSM / H-DIE: gap G-CIL-IDXKEY-FIXEDGO until then). The same net also reaches sm_

.packet: the svg programme gives the SM idle slots that expect the packet (command[29]=1, tag, command[25]=0: no issue, no fault; bench sm_issue 0). key_slot/key_index stay unconsumed observation outputs (the schedule is compiled; the IDX calendar beat = the svg programme slot + the fixed relay latency of the long key_lines edges, H-IDX price +20..24 edges, S2 +0.03 %). KEY LAYOUT (H-IDX keypack/keystore, key_format_v1 service note): pair (stack s, beat b, port p) is the 136-B record at row b of a per-SM key region inside svg_

's own four PCs (record byte 0 = bits 7:0: key 16b+2p = bytes 0..67), not the linear stack byteaddr; tag_base per 64-row block = 128*p + first beat. Throughput: an IDX.INDEX record occupies 171 packet slots of all 32 groups (keys share the SM service). LINK EP (G-CIL-EP): 9 x hfd_ep_static (H-LKEP master, bench PASS + 4 mutants FAIL on its branch), COLL link k <-> ep <-> lk_* in the G-CIL-EP order. CLOCK: hfd_ep_static is one-clock (COLL face and SerDes ck are the same clock) and every COLL clock incl. clk_link is the stream edge, so ep_* AND lk_* run on the stream domain (coll_idx_link.json lk_* clk/rst moved link -> stream); pll_link is then unused by the link group. QUESTION (owner/H-DIE): if the SerDes ck must differ from stream, the ep needs a CDC (off-die boundary elastic is allowed there) and a second clock pin. ep RX block calendar: gap G-CIL-EPRXCAL. RANK: die_inputs die_rank[7:0] (generator patch pending, gap G-CIL-RANK until then). IDX TX: G-CIL-IDXTX stays in coll_idx_link.json (COLL SW needs an IDX source face, see its note). | Codex23:30 integration: all32 svg instances now explicitly FIXED_GO=1. Rank remains the already-integrated cp2 configured operand row (sameactualcol_idx.prm producer for IDXrank and ARGMAXdie_id), no conflicting package driver added. Both rank values must be installed consistently by the compiler. Physical clock/long-wire latency remains OPEN.
notes.sm_vm: X-LOAD TOPOLOGY: one static x-load cluster per quadrant (4 total), flattened from ot_hgi_sm_xload_static_cl2 (wires-only parent) into its hardened leaves (ctl, bfq x4, aq_tree13 x2, bdring = 8 instances/quadrant, 32 total). Reasons: each quadrant VM has exactly ONE read group 2 ("SM xload", 8 banks x 17 b rq / 257 b rr = the cl2 rq/rr widths), and the SM x-store write has no SM-select (xw_grp = beat), so the quadrant x vector is written once and broadcast to its 8 SMs (v14 "x written once / quadrant x copy"). RD_LAT=6 = ot_vms_bank_static rq->rr (n+6) with ZERO die-level stages between hb_vms_<q> banks and xl_<q>_ctl: if placement needs relays on rq/rr, RD_LAT must grow (compiler model tools/hbm_sm_xload_static_timing.py) -- DOUBT, no slot granted yet (compact660_v5 has no x-load slot). xw broadcast fan-out: 2063 b x 8 SMs from one ctl per quadrant spans the SM rows (6.6 mm slots) -> die relays/feedthrough on xw will be needed; the static schedule tolerates fixed stages only if every SM sees the same count (SM front deskew) -- DOUBT for H-SM/H-DIE. eb3e3e94a IS an ancestor of HEAD: attention SM (ot_hbm_accel_smh_attn, kv_desc) is on main but not bindable (G-SMVM-KVDESC). Bank strap masters are leaves inside hb_vms (G-SMVM-STRAP), nothing at die level. fp4 of the quantisers: closed by ot_hbm_xp_aq_tree13_fmt #(FP4=0) (mode = leaf parameter, vmsm 2026-10-15). Coordinator-owned SM ports (clk/rst_n/command/packet/expected_request) untouched; every SM input bit of xw_* is driven here.

notes.su_sfu: SU: 16 x ot_hbm_su_static_pgslice + 4 x ot_hbm_su_static_qcore lifted 1:1 from ot_hbm_su_static_quarter/top (QID SW0 SE1 NW2 NE3 = v15 hb_su QIDs). Params = the only whole-SU proof with the die RF_RELAY: MR1 multirate d9507c056 (receipt results/arch/hbm_su_f2_static_1014/multirate_native_d9507c056: MULTIRATE=1, MLAT=4, ALAT=3, LEAF=1, RF_RELAY=36, RR10/WR7). H-SU branch claude/hsu-k0r2-1705 (PIN_REG lane, programme 7116->7120) is NOT on main and not used. Command source: ot_hbm_su_programme (serial plane, 9688-bit line = 4 x {control1742,vmr240,vmw312,rf54,red74}, MSB->LSB, so quarter q red_cmd=[q*2422+0,+74), rf_rd=[+74,+128), vmw=[+128,+440), vmr=[+440,+680), control=[+680,+2422)); one central instance fans 9688 bits to all four quadrants -- it has NO die slot and its fixed S+4 timing assumes a direct registered boundary, so any die relay on that fan-out must be absorbed by the compiler epoch (H-SU/H-DIE). The stream programme plane (64-bit VM calendar cal_rd/cal_wr) belongs to the VM/calendar region, not here. Quarter glue: red_sel is pure wiring (bound as bit-slice edges); rf_drain_now and the relay head valid were AND gates in the compositions: CLOSED by H-NETLIST/su 10-15 (qcore rf_drain_cmd[1:0] input + red_rf_v output, edges in su.json); bridge_rst_n CLOSED by the leaf ot_hbm_su_bridge_release x4 (su.json). RF relays: 16 routes x 36 = 576 x hbfd_rly_48_<flow> (one register stage each, async active-low clear of ALL 48 bits from rs; the top's st_v reset is a subset, data reset is harmless); ck = clk_relay[w] = serial, rs = rst_n. PAD: stage 0 i[41:48] tied 0 (straps), last-stage o[41:48] open; logical width 41 = {v, addr8, data32} at bits 40, 39:32, 31:0. Flow per stage from su_rf_relays_v7 home deltas (next-home direction). SFU: RTL on main says the core IS ot_hgi_sfu_scheduled_engine with LG_PATH=1+R (ot_hgi_sfu_split_engine is a composition with no own logic; leaves+relays are die instances; H-SU 72130e7c9, Qswiglu exact at R=0/R=9). R=11 per sfu_core_request_v7 (LG_PATH 12; the compiler's SFU_LG_PATH IO calendar must be regenerated for 12 -- only R=9 was benched). SFU relays use the DEDUPE standard hbfd_rly_624 (fwd 596 b = rq34+wq562, bwd 516 b = rr514+done2) x 11 stages x 2 directions x 16 pairs = 352; PAD fwd 28 b, bwd 108 b. SFU core has NO slot (PROPOSED strip; H-SM must shrink SM rows) and the relay stages have no homes -> placement open (H-DIE). SFU rst_lane_n/rst_map_n are given as stream resets (v15 listed them under the loader/CP owner; if a programme-controlled lane reset is intended they move into G-SFU-LOADER). Faults: pgslice/qcore/sfucore fault outputs unconsumed (no die status aggregator in this region). hb_argmax.am_stream gap is recorded here per H-SU ownership (instance is the coordinator's).
notes.vmsm: HBM -> VM WRITE PATH (G-VM-HBM-PATH, static successor of ot_hbm_svc_static_vm_delivery fed by the retired svc bands). Decision: COMPILER-WINDOWED K-PORT SHARE of all 32 PCs per quadrant (option 1 of grants_v7_1925 (3); no dedicated PCs, so SM weight bandwidth is lost only inside compiler-placed VM windows). Per quadrant: (a) vmks_<q><k> = ot_hbm_svc_vm_kshare #(SM=k) between svg_<q><k> and its 4 controllers (engine region, full_die_v16.engine_region): NORM passes the group K traffic; a window command (vm_*) holds new group requests at the K boundary (the allowed HBM flow-control boundary), drains the group beats in flight, issues 16 x len-4 reads per PC (64 slots, address {row,j[2:0],{col,j[3]},P^col^{row[1:0],j[2:0]},00}), steers the 64 returning beats by phase into a Gray SPSC FIFO to stream_clk and emits delivery fills; (b) vmdel_<q><b> = ot_hbm_svc_vmdel_lane x8 (the existing hardened v3 delivery lane, wires-only split parent flattened): landing (begin / fill / block_ready) and the compiler start -> 256 cycles of dq to VM bank b (sector = base + slot*32 + P); (c) vmfc_<q> = ot_vms_calendar_static #(W=89): one programme word per stream edge, fields begin_v[0:1), begin_bank[1:2), begin_epoch[2:18), start[18:19), start_bank[19:20), start_epoch[20:36), start_base_sector[36:52), vm_v[52:53), vm_bank[53:54), vm_epoch[54:70), vm_row[70:85), vm_col[85:89). Compiler rules: begin(bank,epoch) at or before the window command of the same bank/epoch; start no earlier than the bound on window drain + HBM return + CDC (landing start_ok checks block_ready and faults otherwise -- a schedule error is detected, never waited on); calendar_<q> reserves wslot WG+4 (dq) on all 8 banks for the 256 readout edges from start + 3 (lane pin registers). Fixed latencies added by the new leaf: group K request +1 hbm edge, group K response +1 hbm edge (II=1); VM beat -> fill_v: CDC 2 sync + 2 edges. Same window cost on every PC of the quadrant. (d) sfault_<q> = ot_hbm_svc_stack_fault: the channel-pair CA check + sticky fault join of controllers, groups, share leaves, delivery lanes and the calendar (status out to the host status consumer, G-STATUS). Write-back (VM -> HBM, G-DMA) can use the same window: ot_hbm_svc_vm_kshare passes group writes now; a VM write window is the natural extension, not built here.
